long_description:
Alda Rezende Quartet
The Alda Rezende Quartet brings together voice, piano, guitar and drums for an intimate journey through the songs Alda has carried across four decades and three continents. Moving fluidly between Brazilian classics, Latin American song, and the jazz and popular standards that have shaped her musical life, the quartet format strips things back to let melody, groove and story take centre stage.
Alda is joined by three of Wellington's most respected jazz musicians. On piano, Duncan Haynes — recently returned home after two decades performing and teaching across London, Paris and Lima, where he shared stages with artists including Susana Baca and Eva Ayllón, and whose arrangements have graced Bic Runga's multi-platinum albums — has quickly become one of the most sought-after players on the local scene. On guitar, Noel Clayton is a quietly revered figure among fellow musicians, a true "musician's musician" whose taste and touch have made him a mainstay of Wellington jazz for decades. On drums, Lance Philip brings a lifetime of professional experience, from touring internationally with the National Youth Jazz Orchestra to his long-standing role with New Zealand's flagship jazz big band, the Rodger Fox Big Band, and as a senior drumming lecturer at the New Zealand School of Music.
The 2 sets draw on the deep well of Brazilian songbook — samba, choro-tinged ballads and MPB standards alongside Latin American repertoire, French chanson and jazz standards from the Great American Songbook. It's a programme built on Alda's own history: the music she grew up with, performed alongside legends in Brazil, and has continued to explore since making Aotearoa New Zealand home.
With Alda's rich contralto at the centre, and this calibre of musicianship shaping every phrase, this is a set of quiet virtuosity — sophisticated, intimate, and deeply musical. Entry $20

YOGA NIDRA
Unwind from the stresses of the week by finding a deep state of relaxation. Yoga Nidra, or "yogic sleep," is a restorative practice that promotes physical relaxation, mental clarity, and emotional balance. It's the perfect way to rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul: your hinengaro, tinana and wairua.

Yoga Nidra is a powerful technique that directly works to heal your mind by removing samskaras - untying knots and mental impressions. This practice of learning to relax consciously is well regarded as an antidote for stress, anxiety, poor sleep amongst other health benefits.

WHAT TO EXPECT:
+ A 75-minute guided Yoga Nidra Meditation led by one of our experienced instructors
+ A comfortable space to lie down (mats, blankets, bolsters & cushions provided)
+ A supportive community of fellow meditation enthusiasts
+ Complementary herbal tea before/after the session;
+ An opportunity to journal your experience, if desired
+ A chance to destress and cultivate inner calm

Wear comfortable clothes, and bring an open mind, a journal and eye mask if you have one (not required).

INVESTMENT: FREE for AWHI members (on a 3/6/12 month contract) or $25 drop-in for passholders & visitors ($20 Concession pricing available for students, seniors & WINZ).

Want to become an AWHI member to receive this and other benefits? Email us today to sign up!

WHO IS THIS FOR:
Everyone is welcome to experience the profound benefits of Yoga Nidra, and no prior experience is required. For some people, however, Yoga Nidra’s prolonged stillness or internal focus can bring up strong emotions, memories, and/or sensations. You are encouraged to listen and respond in a way that feels safe for you — adjusting your position, keeping your eyes open, grounding yourself, or stepping out of the room at any time.

Yoga Nidra may not be suitable for everyone. If you are experiencing acute mental health challenges, unprocessed trauma, or conditions that make stillness or internal focus difficult, we recommend seeking guidance from a qualified healthcare provider or speaking with the teacher before participating.

BOOKING:
Follow the link to register or simply turn up on the night! Drop-ins welcome.

📦 WHAT'S THIS ABOUT?

FTST is a one-of-a-kind social experience where strangers come together for an afternoon of meaningful, fun, and deep conversation. It’s also just a different & cool way of meeting new people by getting a bit out of your comfort zone and skipping the small talk!

Join us for games, talks, and connections with friends you haven’t met yet. We start with a short & sweet intro talk followed by a few light-hearted group games to warm up. Don't worry, nothing too awkward! ⏰ 3 hours of facilitated and curated activities

👥 A space to meet new people in the least boring way possible
💛 Supporting our mission to slowly eliminate small talk around the world
🎫 Also includes those pesky ticket fees!

We host our events in awesome cafes, rooftops, and bars across the city. We only reveal the location to ticket holders 24 hours before the event.

Of course, in fact, we encourage it! 99% of people do.

We usually get a high volume of sign-ups yet we like to keep it cozy & only about 30 people. We believe this is a good number to ensure an awesome experience! Please try again next time if do not receive an invite - no hard feelings 💛

Silver Clay Taster - Spring
Join us in our warm and friendly studio to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Silver Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. long_description:
But Why, Dad?
Kids ask the best questions.
“Why is the sky blue?”
“Why do we dream?”
“Why does Dad always wear socks with sandals?”

In ‘But Why, Dad?’, no question is too silly, too big, or too confusing to turn into a song! Hot on the heels of the smash-hit ‘All The Things I Wish I Could Be’ — praised as “a celebration of possibility, identity and good old-fashioned silliness” — this brand-new Kiwi kids’ comedy concert dives into the wonderful, sometimes wobbly world of emotions, discoveries, mistakes, and mysteries, with plenty of laughs along the way.

Once again, loveable dads Jeff and Tom bring their “excellent comic chemistry and a relaxed rapport with the audience” to the stage. The live music is a highlight — “catchy, well-crafted and often hilarious” — with “subtle nods for adults tucked among the big beats for kids.”

‘But Why, Dad?’ invites the audience to be part of the fun — clapping, singing, and even shouting out their own big questions, which are cleverly woven into the action.

At its heart, this proudly local production celebrates curiosity as the ultimate superpower — encouraging tamariki to stand up, speak up, and ask questions, because that’s how we learn more about ourselves and the world. Funny, fast-paced and full of heart, ‘But Why, Dad?’ is a riot of music and curiosity that proves asking “why” the best superpower of all — even if Dad doesn’t know all the answers.

Every “why” is an adventure waiting to happen!

long_description:
Raurimu Thunder
Mainline Steam Heritage Trust is embarking on our biggest trip of the year. Modern diesel trains cover this route daily without a second thought, but we are doing something entirely different. We are throwing out the modern dampening, bypassing the mundane, and tackling New Zealand's greatest rail challenge the way it was meant to be conquered: with raw, untamed steam power.

Raurimu Thunder puts you trackside and onboard as our heavy heritage steam locomotive charges into the rugged heart of the North Island to take on the legendary Raurimu Spiral. This is a full day, high horsepower assault on a brutal mountain grade. No filters, no computer assists—just pure, unfiltered vintage engineering working at the absolute limit.

Relax in climate controlled comfort or head to the open air viewing platform to hear and see our heritage steam locomotive charge across dramatic landscapes and tackle the country's most legendary railway challenge. Large panoramic windows frame the unfolding wilderness, ensuring you enjoy every moment of the giant climb in absolute comfort, no matter the unpredictable Central Plateau weather.

How Your Day Flows:
The Scenic Approach: Settle into our premium carriages at your local station as the whistle blows and the journey begins. We steam smoothly through rolling rural valleys toward the base of the Central Plateau. Indulge in fresh barista coffee, artisan snacks, or a local craft beer from the fully stocked cafe carriage as the excitement builds.

Conquering the Spiral: Feel the earth shake as our locomotive battles the 1 in 50 grade of the world famous Raurimu Spiral. This 1898 engineering masterpiece overcomes a massive 139 metre vertical rise through a brilliant layout of horseshoe curves, deep tunnels, and a complete 360 degree loop. Experience the tight, coiling geometry firsthand from the outdoor platform, where you can practically see the front of the train loop right over the back.

The Trackside Photo Runby: Step off the train directly onto the rugged track ballast for the ultimate adventure highlight. Clear your camera lenses and find your vantage point along the tracks. Feel the anticipation build as the massive steam locomotive sets back out of sight, then marvel at the raw power as it charges back up the spiral for an unforgettable, full steam display.

The Atmospheric Return: Board your assigned premium carriage at the summit for a cozy, relaxing journey home. Swap stories with fellow travellers and enjoy a premium glass of regional wine from the salon bar as the train rolls comfortably into the night, concluding an epic day of New Zealand rail history.

Silver Star Dinner Service

As the day draws to a close and the train settles into its evening journey home, make the most of the experience with our Silver Star Dinner Service.

For $26.99 per meal, enjoy a freshly prepared dinner from Hungry Rush Ohakune, served during the return journey. It’s the perfect way to relax after a day of steam, scenery and adventure.

Choose your preferred dinner option when you book, with your selection made and paid for conveniently during checkout.

A juicy New Zealand beef burger with American cheese, grilled onions, pickles and house burger sauce, served in a fresh milk bun with crispy fries.

Fresh East Coast tarakihi in a light, crispy batter, served with golden fries, minted peas, fresh lemon and a house-made dipping sauce.

A delicious vegetarian burger featuring a seasoned vegetable patty with Swiss cheese, grilled onions, seasonal sauce and vegetable pickles, served in a fresh milk bun with crispy fries.

About this Event



Life feels a little better in good company!

We'd love to invite you to join us for an evening of genuine conversation, thoughtful reflection, and meaningful connection in a warm and welcoming space.

The idea behind Good Company

We believe, there is something special about sitting down with good people, sharing stories, listening with curiosity, and leaving feeling a little more connected than when you walked in.

This isn't about having the right answers or trying to fix one another. It's about slowing down, being ourselves, sharing different perspectives, reflecting together, and simply enjoying being in good company.

Each gathering explores a different aspect of everyday life through thoughtful conversation, offering a chance to hear how the same topic can resonate differently with each person in the room.

The topic for this evening is:

"What makes you feel alive?"




What to expect

We'll welcome you with a hot cup of tea or coffee and some light snacks before settling in together.

The evening will be gently guided with a few conversation prompts, while leaving plenty of space for the conversation to unfold naturally. There isn't a speaker and there isn't an audience.

The conversation belongs to all of us, and every person who joins helps shape the evening.

As a special touch, we encourage you to bring something that connects with the theme. It could be an object, a photograph, a favourite book, a poem, a piece of music, art or anything else that holds meaning for you. You're welcome to share the story behind it, or simply keep it with you during the evening.

If this feels like your kind of evening, we'd love to welcome you.

To keep the gathering personal and conversational, places are limited to 10 participants.

• This is a space for conversation and connection rather than advice or support.

• It isn't a formal therapy, peer support, crisis support group.

• It isn't a place for political or religious advocacy or debate.

• Everyone is invited to participate in whatever way feels comfortable. These evenings are at their best when we each bring a little curiosity, a willingness to listen and be a part of the conversation.

long_description:
State-Market Tensions & Geopolitical Rivalry in the Semiconductor Industry
Why are semiconductors central to global power? This keynote explores state-market tensions, supply chains, and geopolitical rivalry.

About this Event



Using the global semiconductor industry as a case study, this lecture explores ‘decoupling’ amidst the complex web of state-market relations.

Most studies of decoupling focus on the United States and China. In contrast, I focus on the relationship between the United States and the full range of key semiconductor producers (Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, and China). I ask when, and how, states intervene in semiconductor markets and propose that while the main actors in the semiconductor supply chain are not hegemonic powers, their high production capacities mean that their power is ‘pivotal’.

I argue that while technology production chains reflect the conflicting interests of states, because production chains also embody key shared interests, states cannot completely ‘decouple’ from one another. Meanwhile, key stakeholders are not always states, but also private companies and skilled workers. These actors have their own interests as well, meaning that production chains become further intertwined, rendering true decoupling impossible. Their resistance to decoupling means that this ‘stickiness’ will be a feature of any state-led attempt to forge supply chain independence.

About this Event



Pasifika Business Fono 2026 🌺

Your business. Your voice. Our future.




Calling all Pasifika in business across the Wellington region!




Whether you’re running an established business, building your first start-up, growing a side hustle, or simply thinking about starting your business journey, we want you in the room.

The Wellington Pasifika Business Network (WPBN) is bringing Pasifika business owners, entrepreneurs, start-ups, and aspiring business owners together for a special Pasifika Business Fono.

This is an opportunity to come together, connect, share your experiences, and have your say on what Pasifika businesses across our region need to thrive.




Help shape the future of WPBN

WPBN is entering an exciting new phase, and we want to hear directly from our Pasifika business community about what matters most to you.

What support do you need?
What opportunities are you looking for?
What are the barriers you're facing?
What would make a real difference to your business?




Your voice will help us shape our next network strategy and future programmes, events, and business support so that WPBN can deliver what our Pasifika business community needs.

This isn't a formal presentation where you sit and listen, it's a fono. A chance to Talanoa, connect, share ideas and build relationships with other Pasifika people on their business journey.




Meet the WPBN Board

Come along and meet members of the Wellington Pasifika Business Network Board, find out more about who we are and what we do, and learn about the support, connections, opportunities and benefits available to you through WPBN membership.




Whether you're already a member or have never connected with WPBN before, you are welcome.




Come for the fono. Stay for the connections.

Expect an evening of:

Talanoa and meaningful conversation
Connecting with other Pasifika business owners and entrepreneurs
Sharing ideas, challenges and opportunities
Having your voice heard and helping shape WPBN's future

long_description:
2026 Taiwan Update Lectures
Join us for three talks by experts on different aspects of Taiwan

About this Event



Session One:

Taiwan Studies in Australia: policy engagement and moral purpose in the shadow of a China-Taiwan war

Mark Harrison

Australia's institutionalised understanding of Taiwan exists in the context of an increasingly belligerent PRC escalating its threats against the Taiwanese. Knowledge of Taiwan is therefore a concern of Australian policy-making, yet in national discourse it remains constrained by questions of defence capabilities and alliance politics. Preparedness requires deeper Taiwan knowledge, able to recognise a crisis, define its thresholds, and understand what is at stake and for whom. This gives Taiwan Studies a distinctive contemporary purpose as a form of critical national infrastructure.

The talk assesses these themes through a 2025 study of Australian public and institutional responses to Taiwan Strait crises, conducted with John Fitzgerald, Kuo Mei-fen, Nathan Attrill and Marc Ablong, which found Australian understanding of Taiwan to be fragmented, event-driven and reactive, with Taiwanese-Australian communities distinctively marginalised.

I then move beyond this instrumental purpose to pose a moral problem the field cannot defer. When the threat to Taiwanese society, to friends and colleagues, is material rather than notional, supplying knowledge and practising critique are not the only responsibility of Taiwan scholarship. I examine what it means for Taiwan Studies to take on a moral purpose, as the discipline through which Australia comes to know Taiwan and answers whether it is willing to defend its existence as uniquely Taiwanese.

Session Two

A Young Democracy Threatened from Without and Polarized from Within

Ching-hsin Yu

As one of the model cases of third wave democratization, Taiwan’s progress toward democratic consolidation has attracted broad attention. Nevertheless, the development of democracy in Taiwan has not been without difficulties. Both external and internal challenges continue to test this emerging democracy. Externally, the security threat posed by neighbouring China, together with the complexities of contemporary international geopolitics, has led Taiwan to be widely regarded as a global flashpoint for potential conflict. These circumstances have compelled Taiwan’s political leadership to seriously consider how to strengthen national security and enhance societal resilience in order to respond effectively to potential external shocks and crises. Internally, increasing political polarization has made it difficult to achieve broad consensus on many critical policy issues. Furthermore, the existence of a divided government has contributed to persistent gridlock between the executive and legislative branches. Thus, long-standing political cleavages, deeply entrenched socioeconomic challenges, and increasing national security concerns have become intertwined and highly politicized. The interaction among these issues poses significant challenges not only for the government but also for Taiwanese society as a whole. This presentation examines these contemporary challenges facing Taiwan’s democracy. Drawing upon relevant academic research and public opinion survey data, it explores the political consequences of these developments and analyzes citizens’ attitudes toward the key issues confronting Taiwan today.




Session Three

Taiwan’s Tumultuous Past and the Conflicted National Self

Rosemary Haddon

The Taiwan issue is a multi-faceted Gordian knot compounded by contested ethnic and political interests, the Cross-Strait relations with China, and unresolved legacies bequeathed from the historical past. Solutions to the issue seem more elusive than ever. All the while, domestic arguments rage and tensions soar. This talk shifts the focus away from contemporary politics to the tumultuous past and the legacy termed the “conflicted national self”. Its theme is Taiwan’s identity formation during the Nationalist (Kuomintang) era and post-Martial Law Taiwan. Stories and novels from xiangtu wenxue (native soil literature) and bentu or pro-Taiwan literature illustrate the way the identity evolved. Further concepts include hegemony, becoming (Japanese, Chinese, Taiwanese), Orientalism, 228 (Ererba) and the White Terror (Baikong), and unification versus independence. The speaker draws on her experience living in Taiwan during the Nationalist era and her recent publication Taiwan’s Modern Identity Reimagined: Becoming Taiwanese (Routledge, 2026).

Somatic Breathwork: Spring Cleanse & Rise
Clear winter’s heaviness and awaken your natural aliveness through a gentle somatic breathwork journey into greater clarity and presence.

About this Event


Somatic Breathwork: Spring Cleanse & Rise





Starts at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

Spring is a threshold, the season the body naturally wants to clear out, lighten, and open.

Spring Cleanse & Rise is a 60-minute somatic breathwork journey that works on two levels at once. First, we clear: releasing the heaviness, fog, and holding that can settle in over winter. Then, from that cleaner, quieter space, we open, using the breath as a doorway into a deeper, more spacious state of awareness.

Because when the body has less to carry, something else can move. A subtle, rising sense of aliveness. A feeling of connection to something larger and quieter within you. Many people describe it as coming home to a part of themselves they'd forgotten was there.

This is that experience made accessible, no belief system required, no experience needed. Just your breath, a safe and consent-led container, and a willingness to meet what opens.

Through a trauma-aware breathwork arc, we'll support your system to:

release the stagnation, weight, and fatigue carried through winter
soften the guarding that keeps you stuck in your head
let a natural, rising energy move up and through the body
open, gently, into a more expansive and connected state of awareness

You'll leave feeling lighter, clearer, and quietly awake, grounded in your body and open to more.

Who this is for

This session is for you if:

you can feel spring's shift but you're still carrying winter in your body
you've felt heavy, foggy, flat, or stuck in your head
your chest or breath has felt tight, shallow, or braced
you're curious about deeper, more expansive states, but put off by dogma or jargon
you want something that genuinely lands in the body, not just another idea to think about
you're new to breathwork and want a welcoming, choice-based space to begin

What to expect

Arrival (consent + information), chair, side-lying, and low-intensity options available
Guided breath arrival and brief body scan to ground and centre
Breath demonstration + choice of intensity tracks (including a gentle nasal-only option)
A guided somatic breathwork arc, clearing first, then opening, steady and body-led
Optional movement to support release (micro-shakes, shaking, or gentle unwinding)
Space to rest in whatever opens, spacious, quiet, supported
Integration rest + grounding
Closing reflection (brief journaling prompt or quiet pause)

Benefits you may notice

You might experience:

a lighter body and a clearer, more spacious mind
more warmth, aliveness, and energy moving through you
a felt sense of connection, presence, and inner spaciousness
emotional release without overwhelm
deeper, easier breathing
a steadier, more awake baseline that stays with you

What to bring

Please bring:

Warm layers (we'll warm up, but your body may cool during rest)
Water bottle
Small towel
Optional eye mask or light scarf
Journal and pen

Pre-class prep

Eat a light meal 2 hours before class.
Hydrate well throughout the day.
Avoid alcohol and recreational substances for 24 hours.
Limit caffeine 4 hours prior.
Arrive 10 minutes early for intake.
If you have health conditions, please check with your provider.
Feel free to email Lynn at if there's anything you'd like to share before the session.

Contraindications and safety

Somatic breathwork may not be suitable for pregnancy, serious cardiovascular conditions, uncontrolled blood pressure, glaucoma or retinal detachment, epilepsy or seizure history, recent surgery or concussion, or severe psychiatric conditions/active psychosis. A conservative, nasal-only track is always available. This is not a substitute for medical care.

Aftercare

After the session, remember to:

Drink plenty of water
Eat nourishing food
Engage in simple movement or a short walk
Journal your insights
Get an early bedtime

Emotional waves may continue for 24 to 48 hours. Reach out if you need support.


You'll also receive a guided audio breathwork aftercare to support you in the 24 to 48 hours after the session, with gentle regulation, grounding, and integration.





Event followed by a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert! All included in your ticket.



About Lynn (Facilitator)

Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner based in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Lynn supports people who are high-functioning on the outside but chronically tense, exhausted, or quietly stuck on the inside.

Lynn's work blends three pillars:

Somatic breathwork to regulate the nervous system, soften protective patterns, and restore a steadier baseline in the body
Reiki to support energetic clearing, heart coherence, and deep rest, in a gentle, consent-based way
Life coaching to translate what opens in session into real change in relationships, work, boundaries, and daily life

Lynn's approach is trauma-aware, practical, and spiritually spacious. The focus isn't on forcing anything, it's on creating enough safety for your system to unwind, open, and remember its natural capacity for calm and connection.


1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching, a spot is open

If you felt a yes in your body during this session, you're invited to go deeper. Lynn is opening a private 1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching spot for someone ready to work with nervous system regulation, somatic inquiry, breathwork, and grounded life coaching support.

To enquire, DM "rise" on Instagram or email with the subject line: October 1:1.

Doors close 5 minutes after the start.
Refunds or transfers are as per Bhakti Lounge policy.


Questions before you join? Email and Lynn will support you.

long_description:
XCOMMUNICATE
The formidable powerhouse duo COMMUNICATE are bringing their clubnight, XCOMMUNICATE, back to Cuba St Tavern in September.

Known for their long sets that incorporate decades of sound, Cyril Orson and Heylady have been punishing dance floors across Aotearoa since they joined forces almost 4 years ago. Since the last XCOMMUNICATE at the Tavern in November, they have launched their label, XCOMMUNICATE RECORDS, with two EPs now out in the wild and more time being spent in the studio writing new music and collaborating with other NZ artists, the project is proving to e a success. They've played sets at R&A, Electric Avenue, CubaDupa, Arkadien, The Mothership and more. With no plans to stop this train any time soon, they are pulling up at Cuba St Tavern on September 12 for another journey through sound

Usually XCOMMUNICATE is a six hour adventure through decades and sonic realms, however as Heylady is still recovering from burnout they’ve roped in two of their good friends, both amazingly talented; Jen Kyle and Hape, to join them.

Jen Kyle grew up on a steady diet of killer music in Scotland. Exposed to the gritty, raw nightlife Glasgow had to offer, she developed a taste for quality sound across genres. You’re just as likely to hear acid lines as you are dope disco, organized and honed into a melting pot of goodness by a critically good ear.

Hape has been rolling dancefoors since the late 90s. He's played sets around the country and had residencies at some of Auckland and Wellington's most well known establishments. Known for his soulful, energetic sound, layered with hints of progressive and always a cheeky vocal, a Hape set never fails to make you dance.

On top of all this, we'll have a lushed-out environment with added lighting care of the amazing Lighterxx.

We recommend arriving early so you don't miss any of the show.

IMPORTANT INFO:

Our event is a safe space for all. If you or someone you know is feeling unsafe or harassed, please approach one of the DJs or bar staff. If you are behaving badly and impacting others ability to have a good time safely, you will be removed. Please act with respect and care for your fellow attendees at all times, no means no and this goes for conversations as well as more intimate requests.

The Broken Heartbreakers with Eigenface
*Just announced, Eigenface will be joining in support at the Vogelhorn Bowling Club show!*

Ōtepoti’s longstanding indie folk favourites The Broken Heartbreakers have emerged from the mists to announce their brand new album, as well as a full nationwide tour this September. Imagine If We Could Just Keep Driving marks the band’s fifth album and debut on Nadia Reid’s boutique Slow Time Records label, set to be unveiled on July 17th.

FULL BAND ALBUM RELEASE TOUR - SEPTEMBER 2026
FRI 4 SEPT - GRAINSTORE GALLERY, OAMARU
SAT 5 SEPT - SPACE ACADEMY, CHRISTCHURCH
THURS 10 SEPT - WHAMMY, AUCKLAND
FRI 11 SEPT - ARTWORKS THEATRE, WAIHEKE
SAT 12 SEPT - VOGELMORN BOWLING CLUB, WELLINGTON
SAT 19 SEPT - HANOVER HALL, DUNEDIN

With the ballad of The Broken Heartbreakers harking back all the way to 2002, it’s clear that the band understand that the finer things in life take time. Their critically adored album How We Got To Now arrived over a decade ago in 2015, with a smattering of non-album singles and live appearances over the years keeping the band in the hearts and minds of their ever-loyal fanbase.

“Rachel and John are such gifted writers, observers, singers, and players,” says Slow Time Records founder Nadia Reid. “These songs are the stuff of life – life on life’s terms. They sound like Dunedin, and Ireland, like K’Road. I’m so grateful that this record is joining Slow Time’s stable of records.”

Music critic Graham Reid once described the band as having “a sound which draws equally on the Left Banke, the Everly Brothers, Brian Wilson, Beatles, alt-country harmonies and the Anglofolk tradition”. The Broken Heartbreakers’ music mixes the bleak with the beautiful, drawing on deep roots of folk and classic pop melody, but with a defiant, subversive twist and more than a touch of modern electricity.

Howell and Bailey’s new songs find them more defiant than ever, proudly redefining what a band known for having a wistful folky element can or should represent. Whilst The Broken Heartbreakers certainly enjoy plumbing “the broken hearted depths of personal despair and loss”, they also gleefully admit that their songs exist to take “well aimed barbs at the socioeconomic wasteland of the neoliberal era”.

To hear The Broken Heartbreakers on record is a special thing indeed, but to witness them live with a full band is a rare pleasure. This September, fans can hear these very special songs live in all their glory, with six shows spanning the motu. As well as the band’s core pair, the full touring band will feature drummer Paul McLennan-Kissel (who also performed powerfully and beautifully on the record), Ayumu Kobayashi on bass, and a mystery figure on keys and synths.

Don’t miss catching The Broken Heartbreakers on the Imagine If We Could Just Keep Driving album release tour; these magnificent stars may not align again for some time.

“beautiful, world-class music” - Victor Billot, Audioculture

Colourful Enamel Jewellery Day
Learn to create beautiful enamelled jewellery with Lisa Sinclair.

Join us for a full-day enamelling workshop where you’ll explore colour, texture, and fire to create vibrant enamelled jewellery in copper or silver.

This hands-on class focuses on the fundamentals of enamelling, showing you how to apply, fire, and layer enamel to achieve rich, expressive surfaces. You’ll make a simple yet beautifully textured pendant or pair of earrings, then learn how to add a pop (or flood!) of colour to bring your piece to life.

Beginners to metalwork are very welcome - pre-formed shapes are available so you can focus on experimenting with colour, pattern, and mark-making. If you have some metalworking experience, you’re encouraged to take things further by creating and texturing your own metal forms before enamelling.

This is a playful, creative workshop and an ideal class for anyone who loves working with colour, surface, and experimentation - whether you’re new to enamels or keen to deepen your skills.

What you’ll learn:
The basics of enamelling on copper and silver
How to prepare metal for enamelling
Applying enamel using different techniques
Firing enamel and building up layers of colour
Creating texture and pattern in metal
Tips for achieving clean, vibrant enamel finishes

The class fee covers enamel materials but NOT metals. Students can choose from a range of pre-cut copper blanks or use their own copper sheet. Findings and chains are available to purchase at a range of good prices to suit all budgets.

Kids aged approximately 12+ are welcome. Any participant under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

For health and safety reasons, students must wear sturdy closed-toe shoes.

Workshop fee $248, early bird $225 till 28 Sept.

Please join Alphabethead and Grecco Romank this spring for a thrilling evening of turntablism, brutalist sewer-pop and dirty, chaotic, electronic dance music!

Alphabethead is celebrating the release of Misanthrope, his new animated music video. A collaboration with Dr D Foothead, the video presents a hunk of organic matter lying dormant in a Cronenberg-esque laboratory. As this undulating subject is fed aural and visual stimulation we marvel at its mutation and evolution in real-time...

﻿Alongside their classics, Grecco Romank’s set may feature primordial offerings from their upcoming album ‘The Heels of The Isthmus’ to be released this year and usher in the full reign of the Antichrist.

More about the artists:

ALPHABETHEAD finds himself adrift in the musical cosmos, somewhere between the constellations of Hip Hop, Electronica and Experimental Rock. As a teenager he won the New Zealand DMC DJ Championship and this title sent him performing across the globe. Over the next twenty years he'd go on to make seven albums as Alphabethead, five albums as one third of cult genre-shredders All Seeing Hand and two records as half of the psychedelic Hip Hop duo Bad Taste. He also contributed production or turntable scratching to Home Brew, Death & The Maiden, Tourettes, and The Etymologists. His highly technical and singular approach to playing the turntable as a musical instrument has led to tours through Aotearoa, Australia, UK and China.

Now signed to Sunreturn, Alphabethead's new music is explorative electronica stemming from sound design, synthesis and manipulation of sound on vinyl. His live performances are bouncy, sweaty ordeals where the turntables are pushed to their very limit. An Alphie performance where the needle doesn’t break or fly off the vinyl and completely derailing the dance-floor is considered a miracle...

https://alphabethead.bandcamp.com/
https://www.instagram.com/alphabetheads

﻿GRECCO ROMANK are Tāmaki Makaurau’s premiere purveyors of brutalist sewer-pop: stitching together opera, industrial rave, and gleefully uncommercial chaos. Formed in 2020 their world is one where high art slips in dog shit, crashes head-first into a drum machine, and emerges snarling, sweaty, and weirdly catchy. For this series of shows, Grecco will be joined onstage for vocal duties by fiercely talented and demonically popular Sean Murphy (CCTV, Boxer Priest) and Princess Paradox.

Over their decrepit six year existence Grecco have released a rapid-fire series of albums (Red Tower, Wet Exit, Arts Colony) that have dominated alternative charts, been nominated twice for Best Alternative Artist at the AMA’s, and topping the Student Radio Network’s Top 10 in 2023, all whilst refusing every expectation of commercial sense. Critics have described their music as everything from “luxuriously bogan techno” to “the rave you never want to end up at but always get dragged into.” Their live shows — part rave, part performance art, part deranged group fitness class — are infamous for their intensity.

﻿Collaboration fuels the band: they’ve worked with Princess Chelsea, Our Carlson, Eden Burns, Lawrence Arabia, Dick Move, and dozens more, expanding their sonic universe while keeping their core chaos intact. Their 300-page Arts Colony book, now sold out, extends their world into satire, visual art, and fictional cultural history.

https://greccoromank.bandcamp.com/
https://www.instagram.com/greccoromank

Journey inward through timeless stories and soothing sounds in an immersive sound bath for stillness, reflection and deep listening.

About this Event


Inner Worlds: A Story-Led Sound Bath





Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

Across cultures and throughout history, stories have guided people inward, offering wisdom, comfort, and connection. This immersive sound bath blends ancient poetic narratives with the soothing sounds of harmonium, flutes, crystal bowls, and gentle voice to create a space of stillness, reflection, and deep listening.

Mats, blankets and cushions are provided but feel free to bring anything else to aid your comfort.





A plant-based dinner & dessert follows the event - all included in your ticket!



Meet Alexandra, your host:

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.


Meet Smita, your host:

From a young age, Smita was drawn to music as a means for reflection and self-expression. During her music studies at university, she was introduced to taonga pūoro, and this sparked a personal journey of reconnection to te ao Māori and her own whakapapa. Following university, she lived in an ashram for several years where she was introduced to the wonderful practice of bhakti yoga. She now lives with her husband in the Wellington region, where they regularly participate in kirtan (mantra music meditation) at Bhakti Lounge.

long_description:
It's in the Ballot - Wellington North Electorate - IN Studio
'It's in the Ballot' takes the format of the Kiwi TV classic 'It's in the Bag' game show and puts a political twist to it.

About this Event



Contestants of 'It's in the Bag' become political candidates in 'It's in the Ballot' Meet the Candidates.

Candidates choose a numbered box which has a question that has been submitted online by voters before the show.

It’s in the Ballot” is a community-led awareness and participation initiative. We aim to increase voter interest in the general and council elections nationally.

By using broadcasting and web-based technologies to deliver in-studio; online on Facebook, YouTube and Twitch; and edited as YouTube videos we aim to enable voters to make informed voting decisions.

This means you can send the weblink of the YouTube Video of your electorate show to your friends and whanau to encourage them to watch the show before they cast their votes.

Enrolments cut off date is Sunday 25th October 2026

Enrol at - https://vote.nz/enrolling/enrol-or-update/enrol-or-update-online

Early voting starts Monday 26th October 2026

Election Day is Saturday 7th November 2026






Agenda


🕑: 06:30 PM - 06:50 PM
Audience and candidates arrive so they are seated by 7pm

🕑: 06:50 PM - 07:00 PM
Candidate briefing and pre-broadcast checks


Info: We check that the technology is working, including those candidates who are attending online.



🕑: 07:00 PM - 08:00 PM
First half of the show


Info: The ‘It's in the Ballot’ host will introduce the local host who joins us to present the questions in the boxes. Each candidate starts with an Opening Statement (1 minute) on why you should give them your electoral and party vote. The candidates choose a numbered box and speaks to the question (1 minute). Candidates are given the same number of questions. Candidates are sent the question sheet 24 hours before the show so they can prepare their responses.



🕑: 08:00 PM - 08:10 PM
Midshow break

🕑: 08:10 PM - 09:00 PM
Second half of the show


Info: Three Hard Hitting questions (1 minute) are answered by all candidates followed by a Closing Statement (1 minute).



🕑: 09:00 PM - 09:30 PM
After show 'meet and greet 'with candidates, hosts and production team


Info: We encourage all attendees to stay after the show to talk to the candidates in person. You may also like to take a photo with the candidates to use on social media to encourage your followers to watch the recorded show before they cast their postal votes from Tuesday 9th September 2025 and must be casted into voting drop box by 12pm Saturday 11th October 2025
